Wii Menu

Nintendo’s console home screen: a grid of rounded “channel” tiles on white, with pale-blue curves and round glossy buttons.

Source
Wikipedia: Wii, section “Wii Menu”
Creator
Nintendo (development led by Takashi Aoyama, Integrated Research & Development Division)
Made
2006 (the Wii launched in the United States on November 19, 2006)
Style
Frutiger Aero (white variant; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Friendly, clean, airy
Evidence
Inspected the non-free 420 × 236 screenshot File:Wiimen.png (Wii Menu after a system update) in a scratchpad copy. Not stored. The console was not used.
Reviewed
25 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The Wii Menu was the Wii’s main interface. Development was led by Takashi Aoyama; the “channels” concept presented applications like a row of televisions in an electronics shop. The Wii launched with six channels, including the Forecast and News channels. Wikipedia: Wii.

Wikipedia names “video game consoles such as the Wii” among the media that used Frutiger Aero. Wikipedia: Frutiger Aero. Avcı lists the Nintendo Wii with the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 as examples. Avcı 2024, “Physical reflections of digital aesthetics”, p. 461.

Dazed describes parents playing “virtual tennis on Wii Sports” as part of the era’s setting. Holliday, Dazed, 2023.

Observed

  • Twelve rounded-rectangle tiles fill a light gray-white grid; empty tiles carry a faint embossed “Wii” mark.
  • The Forecast Channel tile is a saturated blue gradient; the News Channel tile is green with a globe.
  • A curved, pale-blue line separates the grid from a lower bar that holds a thin digital clock and the date.
  • Two round buttons sit at the lower corners: a “Wii” button and a mail envelope, each with a pale-blue rim.

Why it belongs

This is Frutiger Aero at its lightest: white and pale blue instead of deep glass, with gloss reduced to rims and tiles. It shows that the style can be calm and domestic, not only showy.

Borrow

Use a white field with one curved pale-blue divider line to separate content from controls.

Make secondary actions round buttons with a colored rim and a soft inner highlight.
